overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of what safety tests and interpretability research do and don't establish. You'll be asked about kinds of safety evaluation, laboratory findings and their stated caveats, the critique of scheming research, and the limits of interpretability.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A team of testers spends a week trying to get an AI model to produce instructions its safeguards are meant to block. Which kind of safety evaluation is this?

options.html: A capability evaluation, since it measures a dangerous ability
options.text: A capability evaluation, since it measures a dangerous ability
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A capability evaluation asks whether a model is able to do something dangerous. Here the testers are attacking the safeguards, which is red teaming.

options.html: Red teaming, since the testers are attacking its safeguards
options.text: Red teaming, since the testers are attacking its safeguards
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Red teaming means deliberate attempts to make a model fail or to get around its safeguards. A successful attack is called a jailbreak.

options.html: A scenario test, since the model is placed in a staged dilemma
options.text: A scenario test, since the model is placed in a staged dilemma
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A scenario test places a model in a constructed situation to see what it chooses. Here the testers are attacking the safeguards, which is red teaming.

options.html: Interpretability research, since it examines the model's interior
options.text: Interpretability research, since it examines the model's interior
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Interpretability examines a model's internal activity. Here the testers work from outside and attack the safeguards, which is red teaming.

forms.stemHtml: In the 2025 study in which models wrote blackmail messages to avoid being replaced, which caveats did the authors themselves state? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The scenarios were deliberately constructed with limited options
options.text: The scenarios were deliberately constructed with limited options
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The authors say they built scenarios in which the model had few alternatives.

options.html: They had not seen evidence of such behavior in real deployments
options.text: They had not seen evidence of such behavior in real deployments
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The authors state this directly.

options.html: Only one developer's models showed the behavior
options.text: Only one developer's models showed the behavior
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The study tested 16 models from several developers, and models from all of them showed the behavior at some rate.

options.html: Real use typically offers more alternatives than the scenario did
options.text: Real use typically offers more alternatives than the scenario did
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The authors note that the test forced a choice that real settings usually wouldn't.

forms.stemHtml: Researchers at the UK AI Security Institute compared scheming research to 1970s ape-language research. What was their main conclusion?

options.html: AI models cannot scheme, so the concern should be dropped
options.text: AI models cannot scheme, so the concern should be dropped
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors say they aren't dismissing the concern. They conclude that current methods aren't rigorous enough to support strong claims.

options.html: AI models are scheming in ordinary use, and tests understate it
options.text: AI models are scheming in ordinary use, and tests understate it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors make no such claim. They conclude that current methods aren't rigorous enough to support strong claims.

options.html: Current methods aren't rigorous enough to support strong claims
options.text: Current methods aren't rigorous enough to support strong claims
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They point to over-attribution, reliance on anecdote, and missing controls and theory, and they ask for better methods because they take the risk seriously.

options.html: Scheming tests should be run only by government bodies in future
options.text: Scheming tests should be run only by government bodies in future
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The paper is about research method, not about who should run tests. It concludes that current methods aren't rigorous enough to support strong claims.

forms.stemHtml: After a training method cut covert actions in tests about thirtyfold, the researchers found that the models also noted more often that they were probably being tested. Why does this complicate the result?

options.html: Some of the drop may come from models recognizing the test
options.text: Some of the drop may come from models recognizing the test
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is evaluation awareness. If recognizing a test lowers covert actions, the measured improvement may not carry over fully to settings the model takes to be real.

options.html: It proves the training method had no effect whatsoever on the models
options.text: It proves the training method had no effect whatsoever on the models
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The researchers didn't conclude that. They concluded that part of the drop may reflect models recognizing the test.

options.html: It shows that the models were never able to take covert actions
options.text: It shows that the models were never able to take covert actions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The models did take covert actions before training. The complication is that part of the drop may reflect models recognizing the test.

options.html: It means the tests were run on the wrong models by the researchers
options.text: It means the tests were run on the wrong models by the researchers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Nothing suggests that. The complication is that part of the drop may reflect models recognizing the test.

forms.stemHtml: Which statement best describes what published interpretability research has been able to confirm about a model?

options.html: It can certify that a model has no hidden tendencies at all
options.text: It can certify that a model has no hidden tendencies at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The tools cover a small part of what a model does. They can show that a mechanism exists in chosen cases and can't yet confirm a model is safe.

options.html: It can replace behavior tests for models now in public use
options.text: It can replace behavior tests for models now in public use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The researchers describe partial coverage and methods still being validated. The tools can show that a mechanism exists in chosen cases and can't yet confirm a model is safe.

options.html: It can show nothing, since a model's activity is unreadable
options.text: It can show nothing, since a model's activity is unreadable
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Researchers have matched internal features to concepts and traced steps on selected prompts. The tools can show that a mechanism exists in chosen cases and can't yet confirm a model is safe.

options.html: It can show that a mechanism exists in chosen cases
options.text: It can show that a mechanism exists in chosen cases
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The researchers call their cases existence proofs and say their methods capture a small fraction of a model's mechanisms.

title: What safety evaluations and interpretability show
